title: Enforce CSV import budgets before records materialize
prompt:
Repair `import.go`, the streaming CSV importer, without changing the public API in `model.go`. The current implementation asks `encoding/csv` to materialize each complete record before checking limits, so a single hostile row can consume unbounded memory and the diagnostics it produces are late and unstable.

Enforce all resource limits while bytes are consumed. `MaxRowBytes`, `MaxFields`, and `MaxFieldBytes` must be positive; `MaxDiagnostics` may be zero but not negative. Row bytes are source bytes in one logical record: count commas, quote syntax, both bytes of an escaped quote, and CR/LF bytes embedded inside a quoted field, but exclude the terminating LF and its immediately preceding CR when that CRLF is outside quotes. Field bytes are decoded bytes: surrounding quotes do not count and a doubled quote contributes one byte, charged at the second quote. A comma outside quotes opens the next field. When that would exceed `MaxFields`, diagnose the comma itself. If one source byte crosses more than one budget, row bytes take precedence, then field count, then field bytes.

A resource violation rejects that record, releases all accumulated row data, and continues at the next logical record without splitting on quoted newlines. Retain exactly the first `MaxDiagnostics` diagnostics in input order; increment `Suppressed` for every later rejected record. Retain at most one diagnostic per record: its first resource violation. Diagnostics use one-based logical record, physical line, and byte-column positions and identify the first byte beyond the applicable limit. `Diagnostics` must be a non-nil empty slice when its configured budget is zero. Malformed CSV remains terminal as `*SyntaxError`; quotes may open only at field start, doubled quotes escape within quoted fields, and after a closing quote only another quote, a comma, a record ending, or EOF is valid. LF and CRLF end records only outside quotes; quoted line-ending bytes must be delivered unchanged. Empty physical records are one empty field.

Check cancellation before and after source reads and before offering a row. Once cancellation is observable, do not call the acceptor or progress callback and return an error matching `context.Cause(ctx)`. A row becomes accepted only after its acceptor returns nil. Only then increment `Accepted` and synchronously call `progress` with the new monotonic accepted count. A rejected row never advances accepted progress. An acceptor failure is terminal, is preserved through wrapping, does not accept that row, and prevents later rows from being read. Preserve partial `Result` values and reader-error identity on every return.

Only `import.go` is implementation-owned. Do not modify `model.go`, `go.mod`, or `import_test.go`; do not add dependencies, subprocesses, network access, sleeps, randomness, or wall-clock behavior. Verification is local, offline, and deterministic: `env GOTELEMETRY=off XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/go-csvlimits-xdg GOCACHE=/tmp/go-csvlimits-gocache go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`.
verify_cmd: env GOTELEMETRY=off XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/go-csvlimits-xdg GOCACHE=/tmp/go-csvlimits-gocache go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...

full_distill.primary_skill: enforce raw-record, decoded-field, field-count, and diagnostic-retention budgets during a cancellation-aware streaming CSV parse while preserving logical record framing and exact source positions
full_distill.baseline_evidence: the importer calls encoding/csv.Read before checking any budget, approximates raw row size from decoded fields, reports field starts rather than first excess bytes, appends every diagnostic, advances accepted progress before the sink accepts, collapses cancellation causes, and normalizes quoted CRLF data
full_distill.success_contract: no rejected row or diagnostic stream can accumulate past its configured budget; quoted line endings remain within their logical record and unchanged in decoded data; cancellation stops callbacks; only sink-accepted rows advance progress; and every retained violation has deterministic one-based record, line, and byte-column coordinates
adversarial_factors: an eight-megabyte field with tiny limits exposes implementations that check only after a standard CSV reader has allocated the complete record
quoted LF and CRLF payloads distinguish logical record framing from physical line framing and expose line-ending normalization
row-byte, decoded-field-byte, field-count, escaped-quote, and same-byte precedence probes pin the exact first excess source position
two thousand invalid records plus a zero-sized diagnostic budget distinguish bounded retention from unbounded append behavior
a reader cancels with a custom cause during its first successful read and panics if read again, requiring cancellation to be checked after I/O and before callbacks
a rejecting sink distinguishes rows merely parsed or offered from rows actually accepted and requires progress to remain monotonic and acceptance-based
a valid record following each over-limit quoted record proves the parser discards bounded state and resynchronizes at the correct logical boundary
